children.text: Stir together 2 heaped tablespoon. agar agar with 8 tbsp water
Bring to the boil the almond milk sugar vanilla and cinnamon
Stir in the agar and bring to the boil for 2 mins

Remove from the heat pass then leave aside to cool down slightly covered with parchment paper (Will set quickly) Once cooled slightly divide the mix between the bowls approx. 150ml per portion- set in fridge for 4hrs or overnight Crumble
Mix together sugar gluten free flour vitalite and desiccated coconut until you have a sand consistency. Place on a baking tray and cook 170*C for 10- 15mins or until golden brown mixing occasionally
Dice the mango 1cm remove the pulp from the passion fruit finely chop mint. Mix all together and add lemon juice
Remove the panna cotta from the fridge (keep room temp 10 mins before use) garnish with the mango mix and coconut crumble and serve

title: Asparagus Free Range Egg Wild Garlic

ingredients.text: 25 G Herb Parsley Flat Leaf Bunch

children.text: For the asparagus cut off the base of each stem and using a peeler peel from the base all the way down and round. Trim the asparagus so that all the stems are the same size and leave to one side

For the hollandaise sauce place the 3no. egg yolks into a metal bowl along with the vinegar and place this over a pan of simmering water. 3. Whisk the eggs until they have formed a sabayon then slowly add the250g butter whisking all the time.
Remove from the heat and check the seasoning. Finish by adding a good handful of chopped Herbs. Reserve somewhere warm until required.

To plate place a large saucepan onto the heat and three-quarters fill with water. Bring to the boil and add the white wine vinegar. Stir the simmering water around so it causes a vortex and crack the eggs one at a time into the water and cook for around 4 minutes or until just soft poached.
Drain season and keep warm
Drop the asparagus into a pan of boiling salted water
Blanch the wild garlic drain and toss in the melted butter and season drain thoroughly.

Place a little pile of the wild garlic in the centre of each serving dish remove the asparagus from the water and drain well then arrange around the wild garlic place the eggs onto the wild garlic spoon over some hollandaise to coat the egg and garnish

children.text: For the sea trout heat a non-stick pan on a medium to high heat. Season the skin of the fish and add the olive oil to the pan. Add the fish to the pan skin side down gently pressing the flesh to ensure an even cooking of the skin. Season the flesh with salt and leave in the pan until the skin is golden brown.

Flip the fish over and turn down to a low heat. Add the lemon juice and butter and cook for a further 2 minutes Scrub the potatoes and slice into 5 millimetres thick into cold water pick and finely chop the mint and parsley reserving the stalks.
Then peel and thinly slice the onion.

Cook the Jersey Royals parsley & mint stalks in a saucepan of salted boiling water for about 10 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Drain and leave to cool slightly in the colander (for the best flavour avoid cooling the potatoes by rinsing in cold water).
While potatoes are cooling place the onion in a bowl pour over the red wine vinegar add the fennel seeds and leave to marinate.

Turn the potatoes into a large salad bowl drain and add the onions along with the capers and herbs. Season and toss lightly and divide into bowls place the sea trout on top and drizzle with the olive oil. Garnish with parsley cress.

children.text: First make the cake. Heat oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Grease and line the base of a 20cm sandwich tin.

Place the butter sugar and vanilla extract into a bowl and beat well to a creamy consistency. Slowly beat in the eggs one by one then fold in the flour and mix well. Tip into the cake tin and bake for about 20 mins until risen and golden brown. Set aside to cool completely.
While the cakes are cooling make the buttercream. In a large bowl or the bowl of stand mixer beat the butter and icing sugar together until smooth add the vanilla extract and milk and beat again.
Once the cake is cooled crumble into large crumbs. Add the butter cream and stir together.
Take chunks of the cake mixture and roll into balls transferring each ball to a lined tray or plate push a lollypop stick into each then put into the fridge for an hour to set.
Melt the white chocolate in the microwave blasting it and stirring at 10 seconds intervals until smooth.
Tip the colorant into another bowl. Take each of the chilled cake pops and dip into the white chocolate allowing it to drip off a little over the bowl.
Dip into the colorant then stand upright in a mug to dry at room temperature for an hour or in the fridge for 30 mins.

children.text: Transfer the pitted olives to a clean blender. Blend the olives into a ne crumble. Then add the olive oil. Season with a little pinch of pepper and salt. Pulse again until you end up with a crumbly tapenade kind of olive paste.

Place the puff pastry on a clean and lightly oured surface and then spread the top evenly with the fresh olive tapenade. Start rolling the dough up evenly. Roll both sides towards each other until they meet in the middle.

Wrap the dough roll in a piece of cling lm and let it chill in the fridge for about 24 h. Then slice the dough roll up finely using a sharp knife and place the slices on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Sprinkle with a little extra salt. then bake the palmier cookies for about 15 minutes in a preheated oven at 425°F (220°C) until crisp and golden. Remove the palmiers from the oven and let them cool for 5 minutes.

Basil oil: Put the measured oil in the refrigerator while you prepare the basil. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Have a bowl of ice water ready. Blanch the basil leaves in the boiling water for about 10 seconds. Remove them quickly with a strainer and dunk in the ice water swishing them around to be sure they(cid:0)re all cold. Remove from the water and squeeze gently to remove the excess water.

Roughly chop the basil and put it in a blender. Add the oil and 1/2 tsp. kosher salt; blend until the basil is puréed. The mixture will be very frothy. Let the purée settle for about 30 min. Strain through a cheesecloth- lined ne strainer very gently pushing on the solids to extract the oil. Use immediately or refrigerate for up to a week.
Cut the bococcini in half and marinated them for half and hour in the basil oil. Place small disc of palmier and on the top half boconcini and a basil cress.

children.text: Put the ham hocks in a large pan with the stock ingredients. Cover with cold water. Set pan over a high heat and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to a simmer cook for 2 and a half to 3 hrs or until the meat falls from the bone. Leave to cool in the pan.

children.text: Cook the rice To prepare this enticing Italian dish first cook arborio rice along with the vegetable broth. Cook well for at least half an hour. Add chopped thyme and salt to the rice. Stuff the rice balls Once the rice is cool enough add in grated parmesan cheese and mix well with the rice. Prepare small portions from this mixture. Take one portion and using your thumb create a cavity in the centre. Fill this depression with pre- cooked lamb mince a bit of shredded mozzarella and one deshelled roasted pine nut. Repeat the same process with all the portions.

Refrigerate the prepared rice balls Combine all the ingredients and shape in the form of balls. Make sure the stuffing is perfect. Keep the stuffed rice balls in the refrigerator for half an hour. 1L 4. Coat the rice balls in egg wash and breadcrumbs Now beat the eggs in a bowl to get egg wash. Fry the rice balls and serve hot Next in a pan heat 3 cups refined oil over medium flame and add in the prepared rice balls. Fry the balls till they change colour to golden. Your Arancini Sicilian is ready!

children.text: To make the crème pâtissière put the egg yolks and caster sugar in a bowl and whisk with electric beaters until pale and creamy. Whisk in the cornflour until smooth. Put the milk into a medium non- stick saucepan. Scrape the vanilla seeds out of the pod into the milk and bring to a simmer.

Remove the milk from the heat and gradually add to the egg mixture whisking constantly with a large metal whisk until it is thoroughly incorporated. Tip back into the saucepan and cook for 8-10 minutes over a low heat stirring constantly with a wooden spoon until very thick and smooth. There shouldnt be any floury taste remaining.

Pastry sheets - you can either bake 1/2 sheets of puff pastry or cut then bake. ( much easier if you cut then bake pastry) bake in between 2 cast iron trays using baking paper dusting with icing sugar evenly before you bake bake at 160c dry for roughly 12 -16 mins
Wash and slice your strawberries for decoration however desired.

To assemble spread jam on your base sheet of cooked pastry then pipe on creme pat (not to thick) then repeat the method 2 times to create layers garnish with a thin layer of creme pat and top with sliced strawberries and icing sugar.

methodText: 1. To make the crème pâtissière put the egg yolks and caster sugar in a bowl and whisk with electric beaters until pale and creamy. Whisk in the cornflour until smooth. Put the milk into a medium non- stick saucepan. Scrape the vanilla seeds out of the pod into the milk and bring to a simmer. 2. Remove the milk from the heat and gradually add to the egg mixture whisking constantly with a large metal whisk until it is thoroughly incorporated. Tip back into the saucepan and cook for 8-10 minutes over a low heat stirring constantly with a wooden spoon until very thick and smooth. There shouldnt be any floury taste remaining. 3. Pastry sheets - you can either bake 1/2 sheets of puff pastry or cut then bake. ( much easier if you cut then bake pastry) bake in between 2 cast iron trays using baking paper dusting with icing sugar evenly before you bake bake at 160c dry for roughly 12 -16 mins 4. Wash and slice your strawberries for decoration however desired. 5. children.text: Pistachio cake: Start by blending the pistachio into a powder (be careful you dont over blend as the oils will start coming out you just want a nice green crumb). Then mix together with polenta flour baking powder sugar and orange zest and set aside in a mixing bowl. Melt the butter then add beaten eggs and oil. Add the wet mix to the dry. Mix well but not over work as you dont want to develop the gluten. Line a gastro with baking paper and bake at 160c for 30mins on fan 3. Once cooked place in the blast to set before portioning.
Vanilla Greek yoghurt: Deseed the vanilla pod mix with the rest of the ingredients and leave on a jay cloth to dry out over night
Pistachio dry mix for crème pat: Blend pistachio in the thermo mix into a powder then add the rest of the ingredients until a fine powder

Pistachio crème pat: In a mixing bowl mix your dry mix with egg yolk. Whisk until well mixed. In a separate pan bring your milk to the boil then pour over the egg yolk mix. Mix well the add the mixture back to the pan and cook until very thick. Keep stirring so the mix doesnt scramble. Once thickness has been achieved remove the pan for the heat and whisk the cold butter cubes in. once completely dissolved and mixed all together lay on tray cover with cling film and place in the blast chiller. When need for service rework with a spatula until smooth and put in a pipping bag.

title: Garlic & Rosemary Focaccia

ingredients.text: 1 KG Flour Strong 1.5KG Vegetarian Express FLOWHISTR5X1.5KG
150 ML Milk Whole Pasteurised Standard RT

children.text: Mix the warm water with the yeast then add the milk and oil.

In a mixing bowl mix the flour salt sugar and garlic & rosemary oil mix once mixed well add the milk water and yeast mixture. Mix on a low speed then with a spatula clean the sides and keep repeating until you have formed a dough. Once formed mix on a medium/low speed for 10/12 minutes. Once mixed place in a well-oiled tray press flat and cover airtight with cling film.

Once proved to double its size gently place in well-oiled tray with grease proof. Poke the focaccia flat using the tip of your fingers until it reaches the sides. Sprinkle plenty of oil over the dough cover with cling film and leave to double again.

Once doubled in size gently remove the clingfilm (try not to knock any air out of the dough treat it like a baby). Cook in a preheated oven at 200c with 3 shots of steam for 12 mins. Once cooked brush with garlic and rosemary oil sprinkle with Maldon Sea salt and cook for another 2 mins.
Once cooked place on a resting rack.

children.text: To make the brine mix 2.5litres of water with the table salt 15g thyme 15g rosemary 20g garlic bay leave and 4g star anise in a saucepan. Bring to the boil then simmer until the salt is dissolved. leave to cool.
Put the brisket in a large container and pour over the cold brine. Cover and fridge for four hours.
Wash the briskets toughly with running cold water to remove the brine

To make the Dry Rub; combine smoked paprika light brown sugar salt each garlic & onion powder ground cumin and black pepper chilli powder & 15g each rosemary & thyme chopped. Roll and massage the rub until well coated all over.
In a hot green egg or char grill both sides until we'll coloured set aside.
Peel and roughly chop the onions carrots and celery. Slice the garlic

Heat a saucepan saute the vegetables until golden add the garlic star anise rosemary and thyme. Cook for a further 5 mins add the tomato puree cook out for 2 minutes. Finally add the chopped tomatoes 2.5 litres water and the beef stock powder. Bring to the boil and skim.

Place the brisket into the tray pour the stock onto the brisket and submerge. Cover with parchment paper and foil cook for 6-8 hours.at 120*C. After two hours turn the brisket over then again after another two hours turn again. Cover with foil and cook for the remaining timer until moist and soft.
Remove the brisket carefully from the stock and press between to two trays

children.text: For the savarin dough sift the flour into the bowl of a small electric stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment and turn on to the lowest speed. Add the salt and caster sugar.
Dissolve the yeast in the milk then add this to the flour mixture. Turn up the speed on the mixer a little add the eggs and mix until the dough comes together.

Slowly add the melted butter until the dough tightens and all the butter is incorporated. Transfer the dough to a clean bowl cover with cling film and leave at room temperature until doubled in size. Return to the mixer and mix on a high speed for 2 minutes to knock the dough back.

Put the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large plain nozzle. Lightly grease six 7cm savarin moulds with the softened butter and dust with a little flour. Pipe enough savarin dough into each mould to fill it half full (cutting the dough with a pair of scissors to finish).
Cover with cling film and leave in a warm place again until doubled in size. Bake in an oven preheated to 200°C/ Gas Mark 6 for 8 minutes or until golden brown.
Turn out onto a wire rack and leave to cool.

children.text: Combine all the ingredients for the pickled Shimeji with salt in a large bowl and set aside for at least 2 hours stirring now and then while you prepare the rest of the dish.
You can make this up to 3 days ahead and keep it refrigerated. Pierce the celeriac with a fork all over about 40 times and place on a parchment-lined baking tray.

Mix the oil and 3 teaspoons of flaked salt then rub the celeriac generously with the oil mixture. Roast for a minimum of 2¼ hours or up to 2¾ hours depending on the size of your celeriac basting every 20 minutes or so until the celeriac is deeply browned soft all the way through and oozes a celeriac caramel. Leave to rest for 15 minutes then cut widthways into 2½cm-thick steaks and after in square canape sizes.
For the garlic heat the oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic slices to the skillet - they should slightly sizzle when they enter the oil.
Cook them until they are crispy.

title: Sausage roll

children.text: Peel and finely dice the onions. Mince the garlic. Pick and finely chop thyme and sage. Finely grate lemon zest and juice.
Sweat off onions and garlic for 2-3 minutes. Add lemon zest thyme and sage cook for a further 2 mins season with salt and pepper and cool.
Peel and grate apples add lemon juice and ensure all apple is coated.
Combine the sausage meat and the pork mince. Add one beaten egg the onion mix mustard and the grated apple.
Make a small patty cook in a pan to test seasoning adjust if required.
Place to sausage mix into a piping bag.
Separate the rest of the eggs mix the egg yolks for your egg wash.

Lay down a sheet of puff pastry. Egg wash the sheet and pipe a thick line approx. 2 inch wide of the mix. Fold the pastry over the mix. Crimp the edge with a fork and cut remaining edge of for neat nish.
Return to the fridge ensure the pastry is cold before cooking.
Pre heat oven at 180*c.
Egg wash twice. Combine the sea salt fennel and poppy seeds to make a salt mix.
Sprinkle salt mix onto the egg washed sausage rolls and cut into 2.5 inches pieces.
Bake at 180*C for 15-20 minutes on a preheated baking tray until golden. Ensure core temperature has reached 75*c © Compass Gr

children.text: To make the meatballs. Add the 30ml fish sauce and 30g sugar into a bowl then stir until the sugar begins to dissolve Finely chop the lemongrass and shallots mince the garlic 8g finely slice the green part of the spring onion and the 5g chopped chilli then add all of this to the bowl with the fish sauce and sugar. Mix well
Blend the beans in a robo coupe and then add this to the mix with the minced pork to the bowl along with a little salt then mix until well combined.
Equally divide the mixture into balls
For the glaze combine sesame oil ginger soy sauce honey and 30ml rice vinegar in a pan. Boil for around 5 mins to a syrup consistency
To make the dip finely chop the garlic 8g and 3g chilli then add to a bowl Add the rest of the fish sauce sugar rice vinegar lime juice and water and mix well until the sugar has dissolved
Cook the meatballs at 200oc for 10-12 mins untilthe core is 75*C
Once cooked roll in the glaze
